limits: This is contact geometry and finite-pose clearance evidence, not a qualified mounting design.
No elastic contact, bolt preload, thread pull-out, creep or strength calculation is performed.
A ring bridges interrupted support laterally; the existing axial-ray stack failures are not waived.
Ring thickness replaces equal printed thickness. No motor/output datum or total nominal grip is moved.
Ring holes are provisional clearance holes; no machining tolerance or locating fit is qualified.
All 43 manufacturer solids are checked at the source pose; their motion ownership is not inferred.
Authored output adapter and dyno hub are checked at eight angles. This is not a continuous motion proof.
A projected head-footprint witness is an analysis region, not substitute bought hardware.
Contact area is nominal geometric area, not a uniform pressure distribution or load rating.
Remote pairs have analytical AABB gap lower bounds, not measured exact clearances.
No stock washer is modelled without its selected manufacturer model and specification.
No full hip frame, fixture, bearing, dowel or assembled-leg acceptance is established here.

head.note: the motor's output screws: heads in Ø10 pockets, their tops 0.6 mm below the standard face (the link sits on the face; its spigot recess is only Ø40); 6 mm into the RS-04's 6.5 mm threads

axial_dimensions.note: CNC 6061-T6 (instant price: JLCCNC, backup Xometry; exports/leg/cnc/); 8 x M5 tapped 16 deep and 2 x Ø5 H7 dowel holes in the face; sockets for the motor's 3 x Ø6 pins (H7); 9 x M5 x 25 ISO 4762 socket heads into the motor, heads in pockets 0.6 mm below the face; Ø60 j6 journal for the support bearing; a Ø24 x 17 blind bore from the motor side
spec: Material 6061-T6; as machined, deburred; no anodise (it would change the journal); general tolerance ISO 2768-m; threads 6H

Datums: A = the Ø60 journal's axis; the contact face (z 0) square to A within 0.02; the standard face (z 24.6) parallel to the contact face within 0.02; the dowel holes and the motor's pin sockets at position Ø0.05 to A
Ø60 j6 journal, z 11.6 to 24.6, with a 0.5 x 45 deg lead-in at the face end: the support bearing's inner ring (61812), fitted with retaining compound
Ø63.5 shoulder, its face at z 11.6 square to the axis within 0.02: seats the bearing's inner ring
Contact face at z 0 (Ø48.8) flat within 0.02; 0.6 mm relief outside it
8 x M5 tapped 16 deep (drill Ø4.2 x 19) from the face (z 24.6), PCD 50 at 0, 30, 90, 120, 180, 210, 270, 300 deg
2 x Ø5 H7 x 8 deep from the face, PCD 50 at 60, 150 deg (Ø5 m6 dowel pins pressed in)

9 x Ø5.5 through, PCD 36 at 45, 75, 105, 165, 195, 225, 285, 315, 345 deg, each with a Ø10 counterbore from the top to z 19 (5.6 below the face); the spigot is cut away between counterbores closer than 3 mm
3 x Ø6 H7 x 3.5 deep from the motor face, PCD 35.86 at 15, 135, 255 deg (the motor's own pins)
Ø24 x 17 blind bore from the motor face (mass)
Ø40 spigot, 3 tall (general tolerance: the dowels locate the link; the spigot is three lobes between the counterbores and a lead into the link's recess)
Walls of 1.4 mm (1.0 mm to the thread's major diameter) between the counterbores and the face's tapped and dowel holes, 15 deg apart: intended, fine in 6061
